introduction:
A Death Certificate in Tamil Nadu is issued by the local Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Town Panchayat, or Village Panchayat. It is legal proof of death recording name, date, place, and cause of death.

Essential for insurance claims, bank account settlement, property mutation, pension processing, and succession proceedings.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Governing Law: Tamil Nadu Registration of Birth and Death Rules 2025.
  • Time Limit: Must register within 21 days of death to avoid penalties. If delayed beyond 21 days, a late fee of ₹100 applies.
  • Form Types:
    • Form 4: Institutional deaths (Hospital).
    • Form 4A: Non-institutional deaths (Home/Outside).
    • Form 6: The final official Death Certificate issued by the registrar.
  • MCCD Requirement: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) is mandatory and must be issued by a registered medical practitioner.
  • Unnatural Deaths: (e.g., suicide or suspicious circumstances) Police must be informed under Section 194 of the BNSS.
  • Missing Persons: If missing for > 7 years (presumed dead), you must obtain a "legal declaration of civil death" from a Civil or District Court and submit it to the registrar.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Death Certificate

Mandatory Documents
  • Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) / Form 4 or Form 4A.
  • Deceased person's ID proof (e.g., Aadhaar).
  • Address proof of the deceased.
  • Applicant's ID proof (the family member applying).
  • Cremation/Burial ground slip (Crematorium slip).
Special Cases
  • For Unnatural Deaths: Post-mortem report and Police FIR/Report.
  • For Missing Persons (>7 years): Court decree (Legal declaration of civil death from a Civil/District Court).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Death Certificate Download

Note: While the initial registration of death is typically done through the hospital or local registrar, the downloading of the generated Death Certificate can be done entirely online.
Step-by-Step Certificate Download:
  1. Search Portal: Search for "Download death certificate online Tamil Nadu" or go directly to the official CRS portal: crsstn.org (or the Greater Chennai Corporation portal if within Chennai).
  2. Navigate: Navigate to the Certificate Download menu and select Death.
  3. Search Details: Enter the required details into the "Death Certificate Search":
    • Gender (Male/Female/Transgender).
    • District (e.g., Dindigul, Karur, etc.).
    • Place of Death (Hospital or Home/Other. If Hospital, choose the specific hospital from the drop-down list).
    • Date of Death.
    • Your Mobile Number.
  4. OTP Verification: Click on "Send OTP", enter the verification code received on your mobile, and complete the mobile verification.
  5. Download: Click "View". A list matching your details will appear. Click on the correct record to download the digital Death Certificate.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Registration / Collection

Step-by-Step Manual Process:
  1. Collect Documents: Gather the MCCD (Form 4 or 4A) along with the deceased's ID, applicant's ID, and cremation slip.
  2. Submit to Local Registrar: Submit the compiled documents directly to your respective local body registrar depending on your location:
    • Village Panchayat: Village Administrative Officer (VAO).
    • Town Panchayat: Executive Officer (EO).
    • Municipality / Corporation: Commissioner.
  3. Issuance (Form 6): Once verified, the registrar will record the details and issue the Death Certificate under Form 6.
    Note: Hospitals usually initiate the registration process automatically for institutional deaths, after which you just need to download it online or collect it from the local body.
afterApplying:
Post-Registration Steps & Financial Claims

Legal Heir Certificate (Varisu Certificate)

Essential for property transfer, vehicle RC transfer, and bank accounts. Apply via the TN e-Sevai portal. Upload the Death Certificate, Aadhaar, Ration Card, and a self-undertaking affidavit on ₹20 stamp paper. Verified by the VAO; takes about 15 to 30 days.

Bank Account Settlement

Under 2026 RBI simplified guidelines, banks must settle claims within 15 days.

  • With Nominee: Submit death certificate and nominee's KYC.
  • Without Nominee: Up to ₹15 lakhs can be claimed using the Death Certificate, Legal Heir Certificate, and an Indemnity Bond. Exceeding ₹15 lakhs requires a court-issued Succession Certificate.
Insurance Claims

Notify the insurance company immediately. Submit the claim kit along with the original policy document, death certificate, and nominee's bank details.

Family Pension Claims

Submit Form 14 with the death certificate and nominee's details to the deceased's working department. Under 2026 rules, 60% of the last drawn pension is provided as a family pension.
